paper.title_en: Joint Dynamics of Spins and Frequency-Resolved Bosonic Occupations: A Projection-Operator Approach
paper.abstract_en: We derive weak-coupling kinetic equations for frequency-resolved bosonic mode occupations in the spin--boson model. Rather than integrating out the bath completely, we retain these mode occupations as independent dynamical variables whose equations are coupled to those for the spin observables. A projection-operator construction closes the dynamics on a product-spin ansatz and an undisplaced Gaussian environment with a diagonal covariance matrix. The equations are obtained to second order in the interaction parameter $λ$ for an arbitrary number of spins within this factorized closure, and are solved numerically for a single spin. A fixed-truncation calculation using the hierarchical equations of motion provides a benchmark for the spin dynamics with the Drude--Lorentz spectral density. The numerical results reveal a redistribution of bosonic mode occupations concentrated near the spin transition frequency $Ω=\sqrt{Δ^2+h^2}$. We also examine the response of the coupled spin--boson system to structured spectra, nonthermal initial occupations, and slow modulation of the coupling. The calculated mode occupations also allow changes in the bath-side occupation and energy densities $p(ω)δ\langle N_ω\rangle(t)$ and $ωp(ω)δ\langle N_ω\rangle(t)$ to be obtained without requiring an exponential decomposition of the bath correlation function. Its scope is restricted to weak coupling, diagonal Gaussian bath states, and, for time-dependent couplings, the adiabatic regime.
